title: Counit-word augmentation and natural evaluation of a supplied simplicial resolution
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be an ordinary category and $T:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ an endofunctor, with powers $T^0=\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$ and $T^{n+1}=T\circ T^n$ [def-trf-endofunctor-powers]. Write $1_a$ for the identity transformation of $T^a$, including $1_0$ on the identity functor, and $\star$ for horizontal composition: for $\alpha:F\to F\prime$ and $\beta:G\to G\prime$, $(\alpha\star\beta)_x=\alpha_{G\prime x}\circ F(\beta_x)$. Let $e:T\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$ and $c:T\to T^2$ be natural transformations satisfying $(e\star1_1)\circ c=1_1$. Suppose $B$ is a supplied simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object] in $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal C)$, with $B_n=T^{n+1}$, faces $d_i^n=1_i\star e\star1_{n-i}$ for $n\geq1$, $0\leq i\leq n$, and degeneracies $s_i^n=1_i\star c\star1_{n-i}$ for $n\geq0$, $0\leq i\leq n$. Let $A_n:T^{n+1}\to\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$ be the horizontal composite of $n+1$ copies of $e$. Then $A_0=e$, $A_{n-1}\circ d_i^n=A_n$ for every $n\geq1$ and $0\leq i\leq n$, and $A_{n+1}\circ s_i^n=A_n$ for every $n\geq0$ and $0\leq i\leq n$. The family $A_n$ is the component family of an augmentation $\alpha:B\to\operatorname{const}(\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C})$, where the constant object has every operator the identity. Moreover there is a functor $E:\mathcal C\to\operatorname{SimplicialObject}^{\mathrm{aug}}(\mathcal C)$, where an augmented simplicial object is a simplicial object $K$ together with an object $z$ and a morphism $K\to\operatorname{const}(z)$; its morphisms are compatible pairs of maps. Its value $E(x)$ has terms $B_n(x)$, augmentation target $x$, and augmentation components $(A_n)_x$, with all operators evaluated at $x$. For $f:x\to y$, $E(f)$ has degree maps $T^{n+1}(f)$ and target map $f$.

proof.text: Put $R_0=1_0$ and $R_{k+1}=e\circ T(R_k):T^{k+1}\to\mathrm{id}$. Powers have the recursion of [def-trf-endofunctor-powers]. The defining formula for horizontal composition gives $R_{k+1}=e\star R_k$, so $R_{n+1}=A_n$ and $A_0=e$. These are natural transformations: inductively, for $f:x\to y$, naturality of $R_k$ and then of $e$ gives $e_yT((R_k)_y)T^{k+1}(f)=e_yT(f)T((R_k)_x)=f e_xT((R_k)_x)$. Naturality of $e$ applied to $(R_k)_x:T^k x\to x$ also gives $(R_{k+1})_x=(R_k)_x\circ e_{T^k x}$. This includes $k=0$, where $R_0$ is the identity.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, final augmentation paragraph; Tag 016B(3), lemma-characterize-simplicial-object; example-godement-functorial following 0G5N.

proof.text: For all $p,q\geq0$ and all $x$, prove by induction on $p$ that $(R_{p+q+1})_x=(R_{p+q})_x\circ T^p(e_{T^q x})$. For $p=0$ this is the last equation of Step 1 with $k=q$. If it holds for $p$, the recursion gives $e_x\circ T((R_{p+q+1})_x)=e_x\circ T((R_{p+q})_x)\circ T^{p+1}(e_{T^q x})=(R_{p+q+1})_x\circ T^{p+1}(e_{T^q x})$, which is the assertion for $p+1$. The face formula in the hypothesis evaluates to $(d_i^n)_x=T^i(e_{T^{n-i}x})$. Set $p=i$, $q=n-i$. Since $R_n=A_{n-1}$ and $R_{n+1}=A_n$, the identity just proved is $A_{n-1}\circ d_i^n=A_n$. Equality holds at each object, hence as natural transformations.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, final augmentation paragraph; Tag 016B(3), lemma-characterize-simplicial-object; example-godement-functorial following 0G5N.

proof.text: The degeneracy formula evaluates to $(s_i^n)_x=T^i(c_{T^{n-i}x})$. Therefore $(d_i^{n+1})_x\circ(s_i^n)_x=T^i(e_{T^{n-i+1}x}\circ c_{T^{n-i}x})=1$, by the given equation $(e\star1_1)\circ c=1_1$ evaluated at $T^{n-i}x$ and functoriality of $T^i$. Step 2 at degree $n+1$ now gives $A_{n+1}\circ s_i^n=A_n\circ d_i^{n+1}\circ s_i^n=A_n$. The calculation works also for $n=i=0$; no second counit identity or coassociativity was used.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, final augmentation paragraph; Tag 016B(3), lemma-characterize-simplicial-object; example-godement-functorial following 0G5N.

proof.text: The constant simplicial object at $\mathrm{id}_{\mathcal C}$ has identity operators. Thus the equations of Steps 2 and 3 are exactly the face and degeneracy commutation equations for the family $A_n$. Apply the morphism clause of [lem-trf-simplicial-operators-reconstruction] in the ordinary category $\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal C,\mathcal C)$ to the supplied simplicial object $B$ and that constant object. It gives a morphism $\alpha$ with these components, which is the asserted augmentation. Both simplicial objects are already supplied, so the reconstruction clause and the comonad identities used to construct $B$ are not hypotheses needed here.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, final augmentation paragraph; Tag 016B(3), lemma-characterize-simplicial-object; example-godement-functorial following 0G5N.

proof.text: For $x\in\mathcal C$, define $K^x_n=B_n(x)$ and $K^x(\theta)=(B(\theta))_x$ for each simplex arrow $\theta:[m]\to[n]$. Evaluation of the functor equations for $B$ gives $K^x(1)=1$ and $K^x(\psi\theta)=K^x(\theta)\circ K^x(\psi)$, so this is a simplicial object [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Evaluating the naturality equation of $\alpha$ at $x$ gives $(A_m)_x\circ K^x(\theta)=(A_n)_x$. Thus $(K^x,x,((A_n)_x)_n)$ is an augmented simplicial object, and defines $E(x)$.

source.place: Tag 0G5N, lemma-godement, final augmentation paragraph; Tag 016B(3), lemma-characterize-simplicial-object; example-godement-functorial following 0G5N.

proof.text: For $f:x\to y$, use degree maps $B_n(f)=T^{n+1}(f)$ and target map $f$. Since each $B(\theta)$ is a natural transformation, $(B(\theta))_y\circ B_n(f)=B_m(f)\circ(B(\theta))_x$. Hence the degree maps form a simplicial morphism [def-weil-pbc-simplicial-object]. Step 1 gives $(A_n)_y\circ B_n(f)=f\circ(A_n)_x$, precisely its augmentation compatibility. Define $E(f)$ to be this pair. Every $B_n$ preserves identities and composition, as does the target assignment $f\mapsto f$; consequently $E(1_x)=1_{E(x)}$ and $E(g\circ f)=E(g)\circ E(f)$ on both components of each compatible pair. This proves all claimed functoriality and component formulas.

lean.statement: theorem counit_word_augmentation {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] (T : C ⥤ C) (e : T ⟶ 𝟭 C) (c : T ⟶ T ⋙ T) (hc : c ≫ Functor.whiskerLeft T e ≫ (Functor.rightUnitor T).hom = 𝟙 T) (B : SimplicialObject (C ⥤ C)) (hB : ∀ n : ℕ, B.obj (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n)) = power T (n + 1)) (hd : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)), HEq (B.δ i) (Functor.whiskerLeft (power T (n + 1 - i.val)) (Functor.whiskerRight e (power T i.val)))) (hs : ∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1)), HEq (B.σ i) (Functor.whiskerLeft (power T (n - i.val)) (Functor.whiskerRight c (power T i.val)))) : HEq (counitWord T e 1) e ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 2)), B.δ i ≫ eqToHom (hB n) ≫ counitWord T e (n + 1) = eqToHom (hB (n + 1)) ≫ counitWord T e (n + 2)) ∧ (∀ (n : ℕ) (i : Fin (n + 1)), B.σ i ≫ eqToHom (hB (n + 1)) ≫ counitWord T e (n + 2) = eqToHom (hB n) ≫ counitWord T e (n + 1)) ∧ ∃ α : B ⟶ (SimplicialObject.const (C ⥤ C)).obj (𝟭 C), (∀ n : ℕ, α.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n)) = eqToHom (hB n) ≫ counitWord T e (n + 1)) ∧ ∃ E : C ⥤ SimplicialObject.Augmented C, E ⋙ SimplicialObject.Augmented.drop = B.flip ∧ E ⋙ SimplicialObject.Augmented.point = 𝟭 C ∧ ∀ (x : C) (n : ℕ), HEq ((E.obj x).hom.app (Opposite.op (SimplexCategory.mk n))) ((counitWord T e (n + 1)).app x)
